Carcinogenicity can arise through genotoxic or non-genotoxic mechanisms. Genotoxic carcinogens directly damage DNA — this overlaps substantially with Ames mutagenicity but also includes clastogens (chromosome breakers) and aneugens (spindle poisons) that are not detected by the Ames test.
